back: Anything that limits or slows down the production of goods and services.
The emigration of skilled and educated people to work in other countries.
The share of possible output that a factory or industry actually produces.

front: Name six factors inhibiting production in Zimbabwe.
back: Lack of capital, restrictive procedures, skills shortages / brain drain, outdated technology, power and water shortages, drought (also sanctions or restrictive measures, poor infrastructure).

front: Which two power stations supply much of Zimbabwe's electricity?
What date does SADC mark as Anti-Sanctions Day?
Give the two main views on Western measures against Zimbabwe.
back: The government: damaging sanctions on the whole economy. The imposing countries: targeted restrictive measures on individuals and companies.
It lowers hydro-power from Kariba and reduces farm raw materials for processing.

front: Name four solutions to factors inhibiting production.
back: Finance for small businesses, skills training, new technology and renewable energy, irrigation and drought-tolerant crops.
